# Read Gates

This page describes the `reads` slice of the core plugin `claudetto`.
It is for a user who wants to know why a `Read` or an edit gets a deny, and for a contributor who edits the slice.

## The Problem

Three failures repeat in long sessions:

- The user rejects a call in the permission dialog, and Claude makes the same call again.
- Claude reads a file again, and the file did not change, so the second read adds the same text to the context.
- The user rejects an `Edit` or a `Write`, and Claude edits the file again with no new look at it.

The built-in dedup of `Read` covers only a read of the same range (see D60 in [Engine Facts](Decisions-Engine)).
The slice adds a `tool.call` hook with one gate for each failure.
The hook makes no model call.

## A Rejected Call Is Final

A `tool.call` hook wraps the permission check and its dialog.
So the result of `next` shows a rejection of the user in the dialog.
The test is an exact compare of the result with the text that Claude Code stores for a rejection (D61 in [Engine Facts](Decisions-Engine)).
The hook keeps a hash of the tool and the input of each rejected call.
When the same tool comes with the same input in the same session, the hook denies the call.
The reason tells Claude to ask the user, or to use another way.

A denial of the auto-mode classifier is not a rejection of the user, so the hook does not keep it.

## No Read of an Unchanged Range Again

For each agent, the hook keeps the path, the `mtime`, the size, and the line ranges of each `Read`.
A subagent has its own record, because it does not see the reads of its parent.
A `Read` with no `limit` counts as the first 2000 lines.
The hook denies a `Read` when all of these hold:

1. The `mtime` and the size of the file are the same as at the earlier reads.
2. The earlier reads cover the new range.
   Two reads that touch each other cover a range across both.
3. The `tool_result` of each of those reads is in `$.session.messages({ as: "api" })`, and its content is not `[Old tool result content cleared]`.

The deny reason gives the path and the earlier range.
A `Read` with `pages` is not gated.

The hook denies a covered read one time.
The same read again runs, because no hook sees the server edit `clear_tool_uses` that can remove the result.
After a handoff or a compaction, the earlier result is not in the messages, so the read runs.

## A Re-Read After a Rejected Write

When the user rejects a `Write` or an `Edit` of a file, the hook drops its record of reads of that file.
It then denies the next `Write` or `Edit` of that file until Claude reads the file with `Read`.
The reason tells Claude to read the file.
An edit of another file runs.

## Bounds

| Bound | Value | File | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `READ_DEFAULT_LINES` | 2000 | `slices/reads/limits.ts` | Lines of a `Read` with no `limit` |
| `MAX_SEEN_READS` | 64 | `slices/reads/limits.ts` | Reads that the record of one file keeps |
| `MAX_REMEMBERED` | 500 | `slices/reads/limits.ts` | Files, rejected calls, and files to read again for each session |

## Cost

The hook makes no model call.
A `Read` that an earlier read covers costs one `$.session.messages` call and saves the tokens of the second result.
